name: Port Neill
reason: Seaside village with the Eyre Peninsula's largest jetty, 1 km main beach and the 4.5 km Lady Kinnaird walking trail (searched; Wikivoyage Eyre page only mentions it as a bus stop, so the guide source is the web-found weekendnotes/tourism listings). Second-tier harbour town stop.

name: Venus Bay
reason: Town wrapper: the draw is Venus Bay Conservation Park, listed separately; no counted source names the village itself as a stop.

name: Baird Bay
reason: Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula names swimming with sea lions at Baird Bay as a highlight; the bay is the place, the operator's boat (Jones Island) is how you reach the experience, to be said in the bio.

name: Cummins
reason: Tourism board lists the free, always-open Cummins Mosaic Trail through town (self-guided public art walk), a half-hour-plus walk; one counted source, a minor stop. Consider naming the spot Cummins Mosaic Trail.

name: Nullarbor Roadhouse
reason: A roadhouse is a business; searched southaustralia.com and Wikivoyage Nullarbor, which treat it only as a fuel stop and no counted source names a sight (the plain sign is a photo stop).

name: Border Village
reason: For: roadside icon (Big Kangaroo) at the WA border, a classic photo stop. Against: Wikivoyage Nullarbor says Border Village is a roadhouse with little to offer, and I found no counted source naming the Big Kangaroo; it is a business and a short stop.

name: Koppio
reason: Town wrapper: the draw is Koppio Smithy Museum (National Trust, 2.5 acre site), which should be judged under its own name; the locality alone has no counted source.

name: Spalding Cove
reason: A campground cove inside Lincoln National Park; the parks page names no walk or lookout there, no distinct draw beyond the park.

name: Surfleet Cove
reason: A campground cove inside Lincoln National Park; the parks page names no walk or lookout there, no distinct draw beyond the park.

name: Sleaford Bay
reason: SA Parks insider tips name Sleaford Bay Road lookouts and Lincoln NP viewpoints for southern right whale watching; surf beach in Thorny Passage Marine Park.

name: Sleaford Mere
reason: Searched parks.sa.gov.au and Wikivoyage: no counted source names the saline lake as a place to visit.

name: Cape Wiles
reason: Headland on the Whalers Way coast with no counted source naming it; covered by Whalers Way.

name: Mikkira Station
reason: Wild koala sanctuary on a farm west of Port Lincoln listed as an attraction by southaustralia.com; access by permit/gate key from the Port Lincoln visitor centre (cooler months self-drive, tours year-round).

name: Axel Stenross Maritime Museum
reason: Tourism board lists the boatbuilding museum with original workshops and working slipway, open Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun, $8 entry; a real hour-long visit.

name: Port Lincoln Railway Museum
reason: Small volunteer museum open Wednesday 1-4pm only, one counted source; no real chance of a visitor arriving to find it open (rule 4 in spirit) and a short visit.

name: Port Lincoln Old Mill
reason: Tourism board: 1846 Old Mill, the oldest structure in Port Lincoln, free lookout tower over Boston Bay with a rose garden; second-tier town sight.

name: Winter Hill Lookout
reason: Tourism board describes it as a popular panoramic lookout over Boston Bay, Lincoln NP and Spencer Gulf; free and open.

name: Flinders and Freycinet Lookout
reason: Short interpretive pull-out above Port Lincoln with one source; a minor roadside lookout (rule 3), given Winter Hill and the Old Mill cover the views.

name: Mighty Mulloway Sculpture
reason: Tourism board lists the bronze mulloway sculpture by Ken Martin at the Y-Stop Yalata Roadhouse on the Eyre Highway (not Port Lincoln, correct the placement): a quirky roadside icon. Short stop.

name: Port Lincoln Street Art Trail
reason: Tourism board lists a free, self-guided, walkable mural trail through Port Lincoln, always available.

name: Parnkalla Trail
reason: Tourism board and the Lincoln NP parks page describe the coastal walk and cycle trail along Boston Bay to Lincoln National Park with lookouts and headlands.

name: Westall Way Loop
reason: The page now loads and names the stops on the 32 km unsealed scenic loop: Smooth Pool, High Cliffs, Granites and Cape Bauer Lookout; free coastal drive near Streaky Bay.

name: Neptune Islands
reason: Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula and NPWS name the islands as the great white shark cage-diving destination off Port Lincoln. No landing, seen from operator boats; per 'a spot is a place' the island is the spot and the operators are mentioned in the bio. Close call.

name: Golden Island Lookout
reason: Searched the Coffin Bay NP parks page: it mentions only Golden Island Beach in a shark alert and does not name a lookout as a sight; part of Coffin Bay National Park.

name: Almonta Beach
reason: Wikivoyage Coffin Bay lists Almonta Beach among the park's places to go; surf beach in Coffin Bay NP (part 4WD access).

name: Mount Dutton Bay Woolshed Museum
reason: For: State Heritage-listed 1875 woolshed with restored stone buildings and museum, listed by the tourism board, $10. Against: private property, tours by phone booking only and vary seasonally, one counted source.

name: Anxious Bay
reason: A bay label: searched Wikivoyage, tourism board and parks pages; no counted source names it as somewhere to go.

name: Venus Bay Conservation Park
reason: Parks SA and the tourism board both list it: Weyland Peninsula beaches, tombolo, bird life and fishing; free conservation park open to visitors.

name: Sceale Bay
reason: southaustralia.com lists Surfers Beach at Sceale Bay, with lookouts, swimming and surf lessons, 28 km south of Streaky Bay; small coastal village stop.

name: Laura Bay Conservation Park
reason: Tourism board and parks page describe the sheltered bay with mangroves and samphire flats, bird feeding grounds, lookout and 1911 landing site; free, half-hour visit.

name: Streaky Bay Museum
reason: Wikivoyage Streaky Bay See lists the National Trust museum with historic vehicles and local history.

name: Streaky Bay Powerhouse Museum
reason: Tourism board calls it a must-visit: 400+ restored working engines; open Tue and Fri 2-5pm only, so note hours in the bio. Close call on opening days.

name: Streaky Bay Great White Shark Replica
reason: Quirky roadside icon: 5 m fibreglass great white replica the tourism board lists among the town's most photographed attractions; a guide-named big thing.

name: Streaky Bay Back Beach
reason: Tourism board names the surf beach 8 km from town; second-tier beach stop a guide names. Distinct from the Granites and Smooth Pool.

name: Hally's Beach
reason: Duplicate: a stop on the Cape Bauer loop (judged as Cape Bauer); short pull-out, one source.

name: Surfers Beach Streaky Bay
reason: Gentle local beach, single tourism-board listing with no distinct draw beyond ordinary beach time; searched tourism board and Wikivoyage only.

name: Smooth Pool
reason: Tourism board lists the granite-shelf rock pool for swimming and snorkelling on Westall Way: a named natural swim stop.

name: High Cliff
reason: Tourism board lists the clifftop lookout over the Southern Ocean on Westall Way: a named headland/lookout stop (second tier).

name: Streaky Bay Pioneers Park
reason: Ordinary town park, no named visitor draw; one source.

name: Smoky Bay Jetty
reason: Small-town jetty, no named things to see or do; one source.

name: Nuyts Archipelago Conservation Park
reason: For: islands and sea lion/bird tours are a real draw named by the tourism board and Wikipedia confirms the park. Against: boat-only, reached via operators, Franklin Islands prohibited, one counted source.

name: Acraman Creek Conservation Park
reason: Two counted sources (parks.sa.gov.au, tourism board) name mangroves, canoeing, fishing and shorebirds west of Ceduna; a conservation park with named activities.

name: Ceduna Jetty
reason: Wikivoyage and tourism board both name the long Ceduna jetty with ocean views; a guide-named harbour stop, a half-hour walk.

name: Ceduna Museum
reason: For: two counted sources list the National Trust museum. Against: very limited opening hours (10am to noon), small local museum.

name: Ceduna Aboriginal Arts and Culture Centre
reason: For: Wikivoyage lists Tjutjuna/Arts Ceduna Aboriginal art display. Against: single source, link dead, mostly a gallery shop and listing may be stale.

name: Denial Bay Jetty
reason: Local jetty near Ceduna, one tourism-board source, no named draw.

name: OTC Satellite Earth Station
reason: For: tourism board names the 1969 satellite earth station, a distinctive history stop 34 km from Ceduna. Against: unmanned, perimeter-fence view only, one counted source.

name: Nullarbor Plain
reason: A region crossed by highway, not a single place; real stops (Bunda Cliffs, Head of Bight, roadhouses) are separate spots. Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula names it only as an area.

name: Nullarbor Links
reason: A 1,365 km route of golf holes across two states, not one place; single source.

name: Googs Track
reason: Parks SA and a tour page name the 4WD desert track through Yumbarra/Yellabinna to Goog's Lake; a real outback drive guides promote (4WD-only noted in bio).

name: Mamungari Conservation Park
reason: Remote desert park on Maralinga Tjarutja country; listings give no walk, lookout or visitor facilities a traveller can do in half an hour, and access is permit/4WD-expedition only.

name: Lake Gilles Conservation Park
reason: Two counted sources (parks.sa.gov.au, tourism board) name the salt lake and walking trails near Kimba; free and open.

name: Lake Newland Conservation Park
reason: Two counted sources (parks.sa.gov.au, tourism board) name the coastal lake and sandhills; a walk and 4WD beach destination.

name: Lake Macdonnell
reason: Tourism board lists the pink salt lake near Penong on Point Sinclair Road; a quirky natural roadside stop a guide names.

name: Sir Joseph Banks Group Conservation Park
reason: Two counted sources (parks.sa.gov.au, tourism board) name the island group with sea lion and bird viewing via boat tours from Tumby Bay/Port Lincoln; the islands are the place, the boat just access.

name: Tumby Bay National Trust Museum
reason: For: Wikivoyage See lists the National Trust museum. Against: small branch museum, one source, unclear hours.

name: Colour Tumby Bay Street Art
reason: Tourism board lists the town's street art trail, free and always open; a walkable half-hour trail.

name: Franklin Harbor Conservation Park
reason: Wikivoyage Cowell See names the mangroves and samphire flats with sea birds, 5 km out of town; a conservation park with wildlife viewing.

name: Cowell Agriculture Museum
reason: For: tourism board lists the agriculture museum. Against: small local museum, single source, no detail on opening.

name: Arno Bay Estuary Boardwalk
reason: Tourism board and Wikivoyage (Tumby Bay Go next) both name the boardwalk through the mangroves to the beach; a half-hour walk.

name: Cleve Hills Scenic Drive and Lookout
reason: Tourism board (agreed by southaustralia.com) names the scenic drive and lookout over the district; second-tier lookout.

name: Darke Peak
reason: Tourism board lists the Darke Peak scenic drive with the hill and Darke monument; a named drive and lookout stop.

name: Yeldulknie Conservation Park
reason: Tourism board lists the conservation park with weir reservoir and hiking trail near Cleve; a named walk.

name: Carappee Hill Conservation Park
reason: Tourism board lists the conservation park hill with a hiking trail; a named walk.

name: Point Lowly Lighthouse
reason: SATC page: 1883 lighthouse, free, open, at the cuttlefish area; a landmark a visitor can walk up to and see.

name: Whyalla Jetty
reason: SATC page: the only circular jetty in the Southern Hemisphere, 315 m, free, for walking and sightseeing; Wikivoyage also lists it.

name: Whyalla Foreshore
reason: SATC page: foreshore and marina on Spencer Gulf with swimming beach, dolphin viewing and Hummock Hill Lookout; distinct from the jetty as a beach/marina stop.

name: Jim Pollock Whyalla Wetlands
reason: SATC page describes a picnic/recreation area with BBQs, playground and stormwater lakes on a former aerodrome: an ordinary local park.

name: Elvis Presley Museum Whyalla
reason: For: SATC lists a 50-year private Elvis collection filling a home, a quirky stop, free. Against: a private home visited by phone booking with the owner, one source, may not be there on arrival.

name: Mount Laura Homestead Museum
reason: SATC page: National Trust museum in the 1914-era homestead and Gay Street cottage, from $5, open most weekdays.

name: Wittelbee Conservation Park
reason: SATC and parks.sa.gov.au name the headland with bushwalking tracks, seabird foreshore and samphire flats; free. Needs a real pin near Wittelbee Point (Decres Bay Road, Ceduna area), not the -37.17,139.86 candidate coordinates.

name: Point Bell Conservation Park
reason: SATC/parks.sa: rocky point with granite boulders, long beaches and dunes for swimming, fishing and camping; 4WD access only. Second-tier coastal stop a guide names.

name: Calpatanna Waterhole Conservation Park
reason: Single SATC page; a roadside park on the highway with no named walk, lookout or feature beyond a waterhole; generic bushwalking and camping. Searched SATC only.

name: Corrobinnie Hill Conservation Park
reason: SATC page: large granite outcrop with views to the Gawler Ranges, a popular picnic and boulder-climbing stop, free (4WD only).

name: Mount Hill Lookout
reason: No counted source names a Mount Hill lookout; southaustralia.com lists Cleve Hills Lookout and Observation Hill instead (the latter judged separately).

name: Yandinga Falls
reason: parks.sa.gov.au Gawler Ranges NP names Yandinga Falls and the Yandinga Five Falls walk as a park highlight.

name: Kolay Mirica Falls
reason: parks.sa.gov.au Gawler Ranges NP names Kolay Mirica Falls and a Mirica Falls walk among the park's spectacular sites.

name: Paney Homestead
reason: parks.sa.gov.au Gawler Ranges NP names Paney Homestead and the Old Paney Heritage trail as station-history sites to visit.

name: Ucontitchie Hill
reason: SATC page: domed granite inselberg of international geological significance with wave structures at its base; free, climbable.

name: Wudinna Granite Trail
reason: Wikivoyage Wudinna Do: 9 km walk/bike trail to Little Mount Wudinna through Polda Rock reserve, with wildlife.

name: Whites Knob Edward John Eyre Sculptures
reason: Only Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula/Kimba lists it ('explorer statues on a scenic hill', dead link, 2015); a short statue stop with no confirmation it is current.

name: Workshop 26 Kimba Creative Quarter
reason: SATC page: a women's collective of small shipping-container shops with a barista coffee; essentially shops and a cafe, part-week hours.

name: Kimba Gawler Ranges Historical Society
reason: SATC page: Kimba Museum with 1908 Pioneer House, one-teacher school, pioneer store and tractor collection, from $5 (Wed-Fri).

name: Iron Knob Visitor Centre and Museum
reason: Wikivoyage Iron Knob See and the town's own and whyalla.com pages: free mining museum with equipment, minerals, photos and theatrette, weekdays.

name: Iron Knob Mine Tours
reason: A tour/operator rather than a place: volunteer minibus tours leave from the Iron Knob visitor centre to the pit viewpoint; mention in the Iron Knob museum bio instead (duplicate of Iron Knob Visitor Centre and Museum).

name: Middleback Range
reason: No counted source names it as a place to go (searched SATC, Wikivoyage); working iron-ore hills.

name: Corunna Station
reason: No counted source; a working pastoral station without public visitor access.

name: Lake Greenly
reason: No counted source names it; salt lake with nothing for visitors to do.

name: Observation Hill Lookout
reason: SATC page: Cleve bushland hill (Ticklebelly Hill) with walking trail and lookout over the town; southaustralia.com also lists it.

name: Federation Hill Lookout
reason: SATC and Cleve council: 360-degree views from the Darke Peak Ranges via an easy 260 m walk from the car park, free.

name: Cummins Mosaic Trail
reason: SATC and Explore Cummins: free self-guided trail of mosaic artworks through town, a half-hour-plus walk.

name: Gulf and Ranges Trail
reason: SATC page: 4 km hiking/cycling loop at Crag Point with geology signage and Spencer Gulf and ranges views; free.

name: Freycinet Trail
reason: SATC page: 12 km coastal hiking/cycling/driving trail along Fitzgerald Bay to Point Lowly with a 4 km walking section; free.

name: Saltmarsh Trail Eight Mile Creek
reason: SATC: two short QR-guided mangrove/saltmarsh walks, minor local nature trails with one source and no draw beyond them.

name: Eyre Peninsula Railway
reason: For: SATC lists the Port Lincoln Railway Museum in the heritage station, from $6. Against: open Wednesday afternoons only (about 3 h a week), one source, not there whenever a visitor arrives; the name 'Eyre Peninsula Railway' is a line, not a place.

name: Nautilus Arts Centre
reason: For: SATC lists a 100-year-old foreshore building with two free galleries and a theatre. Against: mainly a performance venue and community arts centre, one source, galleries weekday hours.
